hooks.text: A spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid it couldn't close its lid.
Prehistoric space rocks jammed an asteroid sampler open in orbit.
One hundred twenty-one grams of Bennu leaked into space.

title: The Asteroid Sample That Was Too Big
description: OSIRIS-REx grabbed so much of asteroid Bennu that rocks jammed its lid open and pieces drifted into space.

beats.text: A spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid it couldn't close its lid.
beats.visual: artist's concept of OSIRIS-REx spacecraft at asteroid Bennu, NASA, 2020

beats.text: In 2020, NASA cameras captured a terrifying sight: the mission’s prehistoric sample was escaping into space.
beats.visual: OSIRIS-REx camera view showing material escaping from sample collector, NASA, 2020

beats.text: To understand the leak, we must look at the collection attempt on asteroid Bennu.
beats.visual: high-resolution photograph of Nightingale crater on asteroid Bennu, NASA, 2020

beats.text: OSIRIS-REx used a burst of nitrogen gas to stir up surface rocks for collection.
beats.visual: diagram of OSIRIS-REx TAGSAM instrument mechanism, NASA, 2020

beats.text: But the collector worked too well, pulling in large pebbles that jammed the seal wide open.
beats.visual: close-up photograph of OSIRIS-REx sampler head showing rocks jammed in flap, NASA, 2020

beats.text: Fearing a total loss, engineers scrapped mass measurements and rushed to lock the sample away.
beats.visual: NASA mission control center during OSIRIS-REx sample stowage, 2020

beats.text: When the capsule landed in Utah in 2023, the team recovered 121.6 grams of material.
beats.visual: photograph of OSIRIS-REx sample return capsule in the Utah desert, NASA, 2023

beats.text: This accidental bounty held the building blocks of life, which is why the spacecraft grabbed so much asteroid.
beats.visual: microscopic photograph of pristine asteroid Bennu sample grains, NASA, 2023
